deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It continues Gauss's personal register of letters received, headed on the previous page 'Meine Correspondenz vom Ende Octobers 1798 bis Ende 1814'. It is an alphabetical list of correspondents. Each entry has four parts: a serial number, the name, the number of letters from that correspondent, and a running cumulative total. The running total carries over from the previous page, which ends with 64 Helwig at a cumulative total of 415.

Left column (65–98, Herschel to Leist): the running total goes from 416 to 523. The counts in this column add up to 108.

Right column (99–132, Leist Junior to Reinhard Dresden): the running total goes from 524 to 931. The counts in this column add up to 408.

The only 'computation' is the running sum: C_n = C_{n-1} + a_n, with C_64 = 415, ending at C_132 = 931. I re-added every entry and the arithmetic is consistent throughout.

A cross (†) marks some correspondents, most plausibly those who had died when the list was compiled or updated. Examples are Heyne, Ide, Klügel, Lagrange, Lalande, Maskelyne, Meineke, v. Müller, v. Murr, the Rechenkammer and Reinhard Dresden. Lagrange (d. 1813) and Maskelyne (d. 1811) fit this reading.

The largest counts on this page are:
- Olbers 161
- v. Lindenau 120
- Nicolai 19
- Perthes 17
- Pfaff 17
- Heyne 16
- Mollweide 13
- Leist 12
- Kircher 11
- Hallische Literatur-Zeitung 10

Many of these are astronomers, journals or publishers, and university colleagues.

The next page completes the list (to no. 192, total 1212). It then gives year-end summary rows (e.g. '123 bis Ende 1809 748 66,5'). I read each row as: number of correspondents, cumulative letters, and a further figure (66.5 … 82.6). I could not confidently identify that last figure from this page alone. The years run to 1816, beyond the heading's 1814, so the list was evidently kept up later.

The page is valuable for the history of Gauss's correspondence network, not for mathematics.
errors: No arithmetic errors: every cumulative entry equals the previous total plus the stated count (415 → 931).

Possible anachronism to note, not an error of addition: '79 Jacobi 1'. C.G.J. Jacobi (b. 1804) would be implausible as a correspondent by 1814, so this is probably another Jacobi, or the entry belongs to a later update. Identity unsure.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an administrative correspondence register with simple running sums and no mathematical content. Its interest is purely biographical: the relative volume of letters from Olbers, Lindenau, Harding, Bessel, Zach and others is well documented in Gauss scholarship.

checkable.asserts: Left column (entries 65–98) sums correctly from 415 to 523
Right column (entries 99–132) sums correctly from 523 to 931
Total letters recorded on this page is 516

transcription_corrections: Transcription is essentially accurate. The cross after 'Reinhard Dresden' is written immediately after 'Dresd' (overlapping), so the reading 'Reinhard Dresden †' is right.
Entry 106 is read as 'Malthus' (consistent with the image, though the handwriting could also be read 'Molthus'). Identification with T. R. Malthus is unsure.
The cut-off facing page at left shows the count/total columns of the previous page (e.g. 113 408, 1 409 … 1 415), consistent with entries 59–64.
